facts.statement: Date code in this repository uses only UTC methods (Date.UTC, getUTCDate, getUTCMonth, setUTCMonth, etc.) and never local-time methods (getDate, getMonth, setMonth, new Date(year, month, day)), because servers run in America/Los_Angeles while dates are midnight UTC; local-time methods caused invoices created just after midnight to get a due date one day off.

content.text:
I added and exported `endOfMonth(date)` in `lib/dates.js`, but I haven't run the tests. The shell command that would have run them was denied, and this session has no way to approve it. That means neither the new tests nor the existing ones have been run, so "existing tests still pass" is unconfirmed.

```js
export function endOfMonth(date) {
  return new Date(Date.UTC(date.getUTCFullYear(), date.getUTCMonth() + 1, 0));
}
```

- **How it works:** day `0` of the next month is the last day of the current month. That handles December, leap Februaries and 30/31-day months without a lookup table.
- **Return value:** a midnight-UTC `Date`, the same kind `parseIsoDate` returns.
- **UTC methods only:** the repo's recorded convention is UTC-only date handling, because the servers run in America/Los_Angeles. Local-time methods once gave invoices a due date one day off.

I also added four tests to `test/dates.test.js`. They cover an ordinary month, February in a common and a leap year, December, and an input with a time of day (`23:59:59.999Z`). I didn't change the existing tests.

To check it, run `TZ=America/Los_Angeles npm test`. Setting the timezone to Los Angeles exercises the case the UTC-only convention exists for.
